paper.title_en: Near--extremal gravitational collapse in 4+1 dimensions: Schwarzschild--de--Sitter space
paper.abstract_en: We numerically study a formation of near extremal horizons from a gravitational collapse of radially symmetric gravitational waves in $4+1$ dimensions within the framework of pure Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant. Evolution of a regular initial data with cosmological horizon leads to a formation of a black hole with mass exceeding $99\%$ of the extremal value corresponding to the black hole and cosmological horizons coinciding. We demonstrate how our results fit within the framework of characteristic gluing, and present some evidence that the third law of black hole thermodynamics may not hold in the cosmological context, where the extremality corresponds to the maximal mass of the Schwarzschild black hole in de--Sitter space.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文数值研究了4+1维近极端引力坍缩，与黑洞热力学及广义相对论高度相关，方法严谨，且对宇宙学视界下的第三定律提出质疑，具有新颖性。
decision.abstract_zh: 我们在具有正宇宙学常数的纯爱因斯坦引力框架内，数值研究了4+1维中由径向对称引力波坍缩形成近极端视界的过程。具有宇宙学视界的规则初始数据的演化导致形成质量超过与黑洞和宇宙学视界重合相对应的极端值的99%的黑洞。我们展示了我们的结果如何适合特征拼接的框架，并提出一些证据表明黑洞热力学第三定律在宇宙学背景下可能不成立，其中极端性对应于de--Sitter空间中Schwarzschild黑洞的最大质量。
